task.description: WF-02, step 01e — second rework of the design of REQ-105 after the second FAIL of the gate CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR. The next pass is the THIRD and the LAST allowed: a third FAIL stops the run for the owner. So do not only close the two remarks; remove the whole KIND of mistake. Remarks (read the details in the result of the rework-of handoff): N12 (Medium) E2S-19 lists picker.e2e.js but the file exists only from sub-step 4a, so E2S-19 fails with ENOENT after sub-step 3 — the same mistake as N3 one test further; N13 (Medium) the fix of mutant S02 does not work as written: the with-child child writes no readiness signal and E2S-13 has no wait, so the group SIGTERM kills the child before its handler is installed (S02 survived 6 of 6 on a starter, stand-in and test built from the TEXT; with a 400 ms wait it was caught 3 of 3) — the design needs a readiness signal from the child (a line or a file) and E2S-13 must wait for it, with a bounded wait and no sleep guess (AP-144 and ISS-0103: wait for a fact, not for a time); N14 the figures at sub-steps 1-2 are 52 tests, 51 pass, 1 fail (e2e-stand.test.js and E2S-17 do not exist yet); N15 the order CLEANUP_FAILED over STAND_EXIT is untestable — give it a row in section 16 as 'not testable, read by REVIEWER' with the reason; N16 section 18 shows stale prototype paths; N17 survivors Q15 and S19 are informational — say so in section 16. THE KIND OF MISTAKE to sweep, by reading the whole design again with a pencil: (1) every test, table and check that names a file or a function: does that file/function exist at the sub-step where the test is first counted? Make one table 'test x first sub-step at which it can run' and fix every row that disagrees with section 14; (2) every claim that a mutant is caught: could a test written ONLY from the text of the design catch it, with nothing from your sketch (hidden waits, inline commands, a long-lived parent, a warm cache)? For each caught-claim, write down in the design what the test must wait for and what it must hold, and re-run the mutant in a sketch built only from the text; (3) every number: the counts of tests, mutants, sub-steps, the red-after column — recount with a command and write the command. Sketches outside the project; every process you start must be ended by explicit pid and checked with ps at the end. The task text and the design hold no absolute machine paths and no names of the owner's other projects (do not even list them as examples).

issues.text: Remarks N12-N17: all six closed in the design (19.2). Beyond them the sweep found and fixed: E2S-20 read the spec (same kind as N12); the catcher claims S01-E2S-17 and R02-E2S-19 were false; E2K-25 scans only the sandbox flags; N8 and the start timer had no mutant (S20, S21); E2S-11/06/07/08/14/16 had waits the text did not state; the working-tree statement in the header was stale. What I did NOT build from the text: the spec picker.e2e.js (the gate built one for 20 product mutants; I applied P22, P23 with a matrix oracle); R04, R05, R06, R08 mutate the spec itself and stay 'to apply' for TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.

For ORCH (answers I5 of the gate): S22, the order CLEANUP_FAILED over STAND_EXIT, is left as 'not testable, read by REVIEWER' (section 16). The alternative, an injected group-signal dependency in deps (a wider interface for one rule), is not in the design. Default used: the reading by REVIEWER; no record needed unless ORCH wants the injected form.

Anti-pattern candidates for DOC-UPDATER (Q13, also in section 15): (a) a fix of one reader of a file must look for every reader of it (N3 fixed E2K-50, E2S-19 and E2S-20 read the same not-yet-existing file); (b) a mutant that needs another process to have done something is caught only if that process says it has: a readiness signal, not a sleep, and a sketch that waited without the text carrying it proves nothing; (c) a 'caught by' claim that was not run on a stack written from the text is a guess (S01 was given a test that is green under it); (d) an existing guard (E2K-25) was assumed to scan more than it does: read the guard, not its name (AP-094).

Facts the next steps may need: the full npm test takes about 225-240 s on the developer machine (two runs); under the mutants the starter test file takes 15-35 s; a red E2S test of a mutant that leaks (S05, S07, S08, S09, S16) leaves a stand-in process until killed by pid - the final tests should kill the pids they learned from the log in a finally (stated in the waiting rule of 11.1), as the sketch test did not for S05.

Left behind: 75 empty folders sai-outside-* in the system temporary root, made by killed runs of my sketch test file (not by the design: E2S-03 of the design makes no folder outside the root). The permission system refused a bulk delete in the shared temporary folder; I did not try another way. They are plain empty directories, harmless to the check LEFT (it looks for sai-e2e-). The eight old setInterval processes are still there, not mine.
